app/src/main.ts:8,22 — two lines to drop the route
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:120-127 — the only inbound links, in the section that owns them

removability.rationale: Deleting a page is a file deletion plus a route branch; the only cross-references are exactly where the feature belongs. No dead CSS or data helpers left behind (getSpeciesNames etc. are shared, not ability-specific).

evidence: app/src/components.ts:18-31 — pokemonCard is the single card renderer used by all four lists
app/src/api.ts:40 — spriteUrl is the single sprite derivation point
app/src/pages/home.ts:117 — home re-implements cardList's markup inline instead of reusing components.ts:36
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:277-296 — sort snapshot re-parses DOM, so markup changes silently break sorting
changeability.rationale: The card/list concern is well centralized — the Deoxys sprite bug has one obvious fix point covering every list. Docked for the DOM-snapshot parsing, which turns a markup edit into a latent sorting bug.

evidence: app/src/nav.ts:1-14 — pages trigger navigation through a tiny bus, not the router
app/src/data.ts:23-98 — pages consume memoized datasets via narrow exports
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:1-320 — one file fetches, shapes, renders and wires the entire moves section including DOM parsing
app/src/main.ts:17-30 — routes dispatched in one place, pages only receive (root, params)
coupling.rationale: Modules meet through narrow interfaces and a nav bus; server and client are cleanly separated (server.mjs knows nothing about pages). The main tangle is pokemon.ts being a 320-line near-monolith whose sorting reads its own rendered markup.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:16-31 — CardOptions (types/note) stretches one card across home, ability-hidden and plain lists without flag sprawl
app/src/data.ts:84 — speciesFromPokemonRefs unifies the three different ref shapes (learned_by_pokemon, ability.pokemon, type.pokemon)
app/src/util.ts:11-14,21-24 — humanize/enName factor out the two real naming rules
app/src/pages/move.ts:42-43 — count+cardList pattern duplicated verbatim in ability.ts:45-47 and types.ts:59-62
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation (card options, ref-shape normalization, memoization) and stretch well. Minor gaps: the count+list section block is pasted three times and the per-page fetch/404/title boilerplate has no shared helper, so a Moves-shaped Items section is a copy rather than a reuse.

findings.issue: Table sorting rebuilds MoveRow data by parsing the rendered DOM (hardcoded cell offsets, textContent, href prefix stripping), though the typed rows existed in movesSectionHtml just before rendering.
findings.suggestion: Capture the rows array per table in a closure when rendering (or attach data via a module map keyed by table) and sort that, so markup changes can't break sorting.

findings.issue: The default API base URL literal is duplicated in api.ts:7, server.mjs:14 and vite.config.ts:12; changing it is a three-file edit.
findings.suggestion: Extract the default into a shared constant (or read it only from env/config in each place with one named fallback) so there is a single source of truth.

findings.issue: Caching policy is split across two layers — the URL-keyed promise cache in apiJson (api.ts:26-38) and the per-loader memo (data.ts:17-20) — so TTL/eviction/error-retention changes touch both.
findings.suggestion: Keep memo as the only caching layer on top of an uncached fetch, or give both a shared cache with configurable policy.

findings.issue: Home builds the card grid inline, duplicating cardList (components.ts:36), so list-markup changes must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Use cardList(pagedSpecies.map(...)) like the other three pages.

findings.issue: The 'N Pokémon' count + cardList block is copy-pasted across move.ts:42-43, ability.ts:45-47 and types.ts:62-63, so a change to list presentation (e.g. adding a sort control) lands three times.
findings.suggestion: Extract a cardListSection(count, species, cardOptions) component.

findings.issue: The fetch/isNotFound/renderNotFound/title boilerplate is repeated in all four resource pages (move.ts:10-20, pokemon.ts:56-64, ability.ts:10-19, types.ts:29-37); a new Moves-shaped section copies it again.
findings.suggestion: Add a loadResource(path, render) helper that owns the 404 mapping and title pattern.

findings.issue: section() uses a module-level counter for heading ids, making ids depend on render order and drift across client-side navigations.
findings.suggestion: Derive the id from the title alone (with an explicit override param where collisions matter, as the Moves section already does with 'moves-heading').

summary: This is a well-layered vanilla codebase where each page owns its file, shared concerns (escaping, naming, cards, derived datasets, navigation) live in small focused modules, and removing a feature is close to a file deletion. The main editability risks are the moves table re-parsing its own DOM for sorting, the triplicated API base URL default, and two copy-pasted presentation patterns that a sort feature or an Items section would have to duplicate. Nothing blocks changes; most edits are one or two obvious places.
